newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO accuses Israel of anti-Palestinian activity.
newsitem.headline: PLO accuses Israel of anti-Palestinian activity.

text.p: A PLO security official charged on Monday that Israel continued to recruit Arab informers to work against the Palestinian Authority despite a 1993 peace deal.

Amin al-Hindi, head of the Palestinian General Intelligence, complained at a news conference in Gaza that Israel was using Jewish settlements in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip as bases for a network of Arab informers.

"Israel is planting collaborators to provide it with information. It is also operating economic spies to smuggle in stolen cars and rotten food," Hindi said. "The settlements scattered around the Palestinian self-rule areas are used for spying and to employ collaborators and for activities against the Palestinian Authority."

Israeli security sources confirmed that the Israeli secret service operates stations from some of the more than 100 settlements scattered across the West Bank and Gaza Strip but denied that collaborators are involved in smuggling.
"Collaborators are only used for gathering intelligence information," one security source told Reuters.
Israel relied heavily on local Palestinians, recruited and trained to work as informers, before the landmark 1993 self-rule accord with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.

Hundreds of suspected informers were killed by activists of an uprising which began in 1987 and tapered off when the peace deal was signed. Hundreds more took refuge in Israel with their families after the accord, fearing revenge.

Hindi said Palestinian security forces had detained more than 100 collaborators who had been recruited since the accord. He said Israel usually "extorts" Palestinians applying for job permits in Israel to work for its Shin Bet secret service.
